# Quickwell: full page list

> Every reference page on Quickwell with a one-line summary. See https://quickwell.app/llms.txt for the overview.

## Tools

- [Rate Con Checker](https://quickwell.app/rate-con-checker/): Paste a trucking broker rate confirmation; 20 checks (detention, TONU, layover, lumper, fines, setoff, payment terms, broker identity and more) give a grade and a ready-to-send fix request. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded. 3 free checks a day; Pro is $9/month or $79/year.
- [New Authority Audit Kit](https://quickwell.app/audit-kit/): Free self-check against the 16 violations that automatically fail an FMCSA new entrant safety audit (49 CFR 385.321(b)), then an optional $39 one-time kit that fills in driver files, drug and alcohol program documents, maintenance files and an audit binder. Runs in the browser.
- [EUDR Plot File Checker](https://quickwell.app/plot-file-checker/): Free checker for farm plot geolocation files (GeoJSON, KML, CSV, WKT) under the EU Deforestation Regulation; flags the EU Information System's file rules and fixes the safe ones. English and French. Runs in the browser.
- [Permit Watch (Texas)](https://quickwell.app/permit-watch/): Free list of new Texas drilling permits by county from the Railroad Commission of Texas daily permit file, with filters and a free RSS feed per county. First data load pending.

## Rate con glossary

- [Rate confirmation glossary: the terms that cost truckers money](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/): Plain-English definitions of rate confirmation terms: detention, TONU, layover, lumper, setoff, quick pay, factoring and NOA, double brokering, claims and more, with what to ask a broker before you sign.
- [Rate confirmation (rate con)](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/rate-confirmation/): A rate confirmation is the load-by-load contract between a carrier and a broker. Learn what it should contain, why the signed paper beats the phone call, and what to check first.
- [Detention](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/detention/): What detention means on a rate confirmation, how free time and the hourly rate work, why waiting time eats your hours of service, and the exact wording to ask a broker for.
- [TONU (truck ordered, not used)](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/tonu/): TONU means truck ordered, not used: a flat fee a broker pays when a load is cancelled after the carrier is dispatched. What to look for in the wording and how to make it enforceable.
- [Layover](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/layover/): Layover pay compensates a carrier when a truck is held overnight or a load is pushed to the next day. How it differs from detention, how it interacts with hours of service, and what to ask for.
- [Lumper fee](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/lumper/): A lumper is a third-party crew that unloads trucks at a warehouse. Learn how lumper fees are paid, the rate con wording that makes them your cost, and how to get reimbursed quickly.
- [Accessorial charges](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/accessorial/): Accessorials are the charges on top of line haul: detention, layover, TONU, lumper, extra stops, driver assist and more. Why they must be written on the rate con and how to get them paid.
- [Fuel surcharge (FSC)](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/fuel-surcharge/): What a fuel surcharge (FSC) line means on a broker rate confirmation, how it differs from an all-in rate, and how to compare loads fairly per mile when fuel is included.
- [Quick pay](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/quick-pay/): Quick pay lets a carrier get paid by the broker in days instead of 30 to 45 days, for a percentage fee. How to calculate the true cost, what to read in the terms, and how it compares with factoring.
- [Factoring and notice of assignment (NOA)](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/factoring-noa/): How freight factoring works, what a notice of assignment (NOA) does, why a broker may refuse to pay you directly, and the rate con clauses that interact with factoring.
- [Double brokering](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/double-brokering/): Double brokering is when a load is passed on to another carrier without authority or consent. What federal rules say about brokers, the $75,000 broker bond, and warning signs on a rate con.
- [Setoff (offset) clause](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/setoff/): A setoff or offset clause lets a broker deduct money it claims you owe from pay on other loads, including disputed claims. Why it is risky, wording to watch for, and what to ask for instead.
- [Fines, deductions and chargebacks](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/fines-deductions/): Fines and chargebacks on rate confirmations: late-delivery penalties, missing-paperwork deductions, tracking fines. How to find every dollar amount before you sign and what to ask a broker to remove.
- [Check calls](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/check-calls/): Check calls are the status updates a broker requires during a load. What rate cons typically demand, how check-call penalties work, and the federal hand-held phone and texting rules drivers must follow.
- [Tracking app requirements](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/tracking-apps/): Why brokers require tracking apps like MacroPoint, Trucker Tools, FourKites or project44, how tracking fines work, and what to ask for so a tracking gap doesn't cost you an on-time load.
- [FCFS vs. appointment](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/fcfs-vs-appointment/): FCFS (first come, first served) means arrive any time within a window; an appointment is a set time. Why mixed scheduling terms on a rate con cause missed loads, fines and unpaid waiting.
- [Reefer temperature clause](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/reefer-temperature/): For refrigerated loads, the rate con should state the temperature set point and whether the unit runs continuous or cycle. Why a missing temperature turns a rejected load into the carrier's problem.
- [Cargo claims and liability](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/cargo-claims/): How cargo claims work for carriers: the federal claim filing and response timelines (30 and 120 days), cargo value versus your insurance limit, and rate con clauses that deduct claims from freight pay.
- [Payment terms (net 30, net 45)](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/payment-terms/): What net 30, net 45 and similar payment terms mean on a broker rate confirmation, when the clock starts, what "clean paperwork" means, and how long terms cost a carrier in cash flow.
- [Indemnity clause](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/indemnity/): An indemnity clause decides who pays if a claim or lawsuit arises from a load. Why one-way, carrier-only indemnity is risky, what mutual wording looks like, and what to ask for.
- [Arbitration and venue clauses](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/arbitration-venue/): Rate cons often say disputes go to binding arbitration or a court in the broker's home county. What governing law, venue and arbitration clauses mean for a small carrier chasing an unpaid load.
- [Driver assist / driver unload](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/driver-assist/): Driver assist, driver unload, tailgate and freight-count requirements mean the driver works the dock. What the terms mean, how they affect hours of service, and how to make sure the work is paid.
- [Rate adjustment clause](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/rate-changes/): Some rate cons let the broker adjust or reduce the rate after signing. What "rate subject to change" wording looks like, why it undermines the whole contract, and what to ask for.
- [Sign-by deadline](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/sign-by-deadline/): Short sign-by deadlines on rate confirmations push carriers to sign without reading. Why they appear, why they also show up in fraud, and a fast routine for reading a rate con in five minutes.
- [Broker MC/DOT verification](https://quickwell.app/learn/rate-con/broker-verification/): Before hauling for a broker, check its MC and USDOT numbers on FMCSA's public record, its authority and bond, and its contact details. Warning signs on a rate con and what federal rules require of brokers.

## New entrant audit

- [The 16 violations that automatically fail an FMCSA new entrant safety audit](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/): Every automatic-fail violation in the FMCSA new entrant safety audit (49 CFR 385.321(b)), one page each: what the rule says, the records involved, how to fix it, and the audit timeline.
- [Row 1: No drug and alcohol testing program (49 CFR 382.115)](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/drug-alcohol-testing-program/): Automatic-fail row 1 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: no DOT drug and alcohol testing program when CMV operations began (49 CFR 382.115). What the rule requires, records auditors look at, and how to fix it.
- [Row 2: Using a driver with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or greater (49 CFR 382.201)](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/alcohol-0-04/): Automatic-fail row 2 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: letting a driver known to have an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or greater perform safety-sensitive functions (49 CFR 382.201).
- [Row 3: Using a driver who refused a required drug or alcohol test (49 CFR 382.211)](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/refused-test/): Automatic-fail row 3 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: letting a driver who refused a required Part 382 drug or alcohol test keep doing safety-sensitive work (49 CFR 382.211).
- [Row 4: Using a driver known to have tested positive for drugs (49 CFR 382.215)](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/positive-drug-test/): Automatic-fail row 4 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: letting a driver known to have tested positive (or adulterated or substituted a specimen) perform safety-sensitive functions (49 CFR 382.215).
- [Row 5: No random drug and alcohol testing program (49 CFR 382.305)](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/random-testing/): Automatic-fail row 5 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: no random controlled substances and alcohol testing program (49 CFR 382.305). Pools, selection rules, rates and the records that prove it.
- [Row 6: Knowingly using a driver without a valid CDL (49 CFR 383.3(a) / 383.23(a))](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/no-valid-cdl/): Automatic-fail row 6 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: knowingly using a driver who does not possess a valid CDL (49 CFR 383.3(a), 383.23(a)). Class, endorsements, CLP limits and the records to keep.
- [Row 7: Using a driver whose CDL or CLP is disqualified, or who lost the right to drive a CMV (49 CFR 383.37(b))](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/disqualified-cdl-or-clp/): Automatic-fail row 7 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: allowing a driver whose CDL or CLP is disqualified by a State, or who has lost the right to operate a CMV in a State, to drive (49 CFR 383.37(b)).
- [Row 8: Letting a driver disqualified under the CDL rules drive (49 CFR 383.51(a))](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/cdl-disqualified-driver/): Automatic-fail row 8 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: knowingly allowing a driver disqualified under 49 CFR 383.51 to drive a CMV. The disqualifying offenses, periods and how carriers stay compliant.
- [Row 9: Operating without required minimum insurance (49 CFR 387.7(a))](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/insurance-property-carriers/): Automatic-fail row 9 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: operating a motor vehicle without the required minimum levels of financial responsibility (49 CFR 387.7, limits in 387.9). Limits, MCS-90 and lapses.
- [Row 10: Operating a passenger vehicle without required minimum insurance (49 CFR 387.31(a))](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/insurance-passenger-carriers/): Automatic-fail row 10 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: operating a passenger-carrying vehicle without the required minimum financial responsibility (49 CFR 387.31, limits in 387.33T). Limits and MCS-90B.
- [Row 11: Knowingly using a disqualified driver (49 CFR 391.15(a))](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/disqualified-driver/): Automatic-fail row 11 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: using a driver disqualified under 49 CFR 391.15, which applies to CDL and non-CDL drivers alike. Grounds, periods and the records that catch it.
- [Row 12: Knowingly using a physically unqualified driver (49 CFR 391.11(b)(4))](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/medical-certificate/): Automatic-fail row 12 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: using a driver who is not physically qualified, usually one with no current DOT medical certificate (49 CFR 391.11(b)(4), 391.41, 391.45).
- [Row 13: Failing to require a record of duty status (49 CFR 395.8(a))](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/hours-of-service-records/): Automatic-fail row 13 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: failing to require drivers to record duty status, with a 51% threshold (49 CFR 395.8(a)). ELDs, paper-log exceptions, short-haul and retention.
- [Row 14: Operating a vehicle declared out of service before repairs (49 CFR 396.9(c)(2))](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/out-of-service-vehicle/): Automatic-fail row 14 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: requiring or permitting operation of a CMV declared out of service before the repairs are made (49 CFR 396.9(c)(2)). Towing, certification and records.
- [Row 15: Not fixing out-of-service defects on a driver vehicle inspection report (49 CFR 396.11(a)(3))](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/dvir-defects/): Automatic-fail row 15 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: failing to correct out-of-service defects listed by a driver on a DVIR before the vehicle is operated (49 CFR 396.11(a)(3)). Reports, repairs, certification.
- [Row 16: Using a CMV not periodically inspected (49 CFR 396.17(a))](https://quickwell.app/learn/new-entrant-audit/annual-inspection/): Automatic-fail row 16 of the FMCSA new entrant audit: using CMVs not periodically inspected, with a 51% threshold (49 CFR 396.17(a)). Every unit in a combination, qualified inspectors, proof on the vehicle, 14-month records.

## EUDR plot file errors

- [EUDR plot file errors, and how to fix each one](https://quickwell.app/learn/eudr/): The common reasons an EUDR geolocation (GeoJSON) file is rejected by the EU Information System: swapped coordinates, decimals, open or self-crossing polygons, holes, points over 4 ha, file size, property names. One page each.
- [Wrong coordinate system: EUDR files must be WGS 84 longitude/latitude](https://quickwell.app/learn/eudr/coordinate-system-wgs84/): The EU Information System accepts plot coordinates only in WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), in decimal degrees, longitude first. How to spot projected (metre) coordinates, out-of-range values and 0,0 points, and how to convert.
- [Swapped coordinates: latitude and longitude in the wrong order](https://quickwell.app/learn/eudr/swapped-coordinates/): In GeoJSON, each position is [longitude, latitude]. Files built from spreadsheets often reverse it, putting plots in the wrong country or the sea. How to spot swapped EUDR coordinates and fix them safely.
- [Decimal places: at least 6, and what truncation does to your polygons](https://quickwell.app/learn/eudr/six-decimal-places/): EUDR geolocation needs at least 6 decimal digits, and the EU Information System truncates anything beyond 6. Why too few decimals fail, how truncation can create duplicate points, and what to do.
- [Unclosed polygon: the first and last point must be the same](https://quickwell.app/learn/eudr/unclosed-polygon/): Every EUDR plot polygon must be closed: the first and last coordinate pair must be identical, and a polygon needs at least four positions. Why polygons come out open and how to close them.
- [Self-intersecting polygon: crossing lines, figure-eights and spikes](https://quickwell.app/learn/eudr/self-intersecting-polygon/): The EU Information System rejects plot polygons whose edges cross (figure-eight shapes), fold back over themselves or form spikes. Why these shapes happen, why they can't be auto-fixed, and how to re-map them.
- [Polygons with holes are not accepted: the two-halves workaround](https://quickwell.app/learn/eudr/polygon-holes/): The EU Information System does not accept polygons with holes (doughnut shapes). Why plots end up with holes and the official workaround: describe the plot as two half-doughnut polygons.
- [Points and the 4-hectare rule: when a plot needs a polygon](https://quickwell.app/learn/eudr/point-area-over-4-hectares/): In EUDR geolocation, a single point may stand for a plot of up to 4 hectares; larger plots need a polygon, except for cattle. How the EU Information System reads the Area property, its 4 ha default and its minimum.
- [LineString and MultiLineString are not accepted for plots](https://quickwell.app/learn/eudr/linestring-not-accepted/): The EU Information System does not accept LineString or MultiLineString geometries for production places. Why GPS apps export lines, and how to turn a walked boundary into a valid polygon.
- [GeometryCollection in EUDR files: accepted, but check what's inside](https://quickwell.app/learn/eudr/geometrycollection/): The EU Information System accepts GeometryCollection, but a collection containing lines, or mixing points and polygons, causes errors and confusion. How to replace a GeometryCollection with MultiPolygon or MultiPoint.
- [Property names: ProducerName, ProducerCountry, ProductionPlace, Area](https://quickwell.app/learn/eudr/property-names/): The EU Information System reads four optional GeoJSON properties, with case-sensitive names: ProducerName, ProducerCountry (ISO 2-letter code), ProductionPlace and Area. Common naming mistakes and how to fix them.
- [File size and volume limits: 25 MB per statement, 1,000 producers per commodity](https://quickwell.app/learn/eudr/file-size-limit/): The EU Information System limits geolocation data to 25 MB per due diligence statement, and producers to 1,000 per commodity and 10,000 per statement. How to shrink a plot file without losing accuracy.

## Erreurs de fichiers RDUE (French)

- [Erreurs des fichiers de parcelles RDUE, et comment corriger chacune](https://quickwell.app/fr/learn/eudr/): Pourquoi un fichier de géolocalisation RDUE (GeoJSON) est refusé par le Système d'information de l'UE : coordonnées inversées, décimales, polygones ouverts ou croisés, trous, points de plus de 4 ha, taille, noms de propriétés.
- [Mauvais système de coordonnées : les fichiers RDUE doivent être en WGS 84 longitude/latitude](https://quickwell.app/fr/learn/eudr/coordinate-system-wgs84/): Le Système d'information de l'UE n'accepte les coordonnées des parcelles qu'en WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), en degrés décimaux, longitude d'abord. Comment repérer des coordonnées en mètres, hors limites ou à 0,0, et comment les convertir.
- [Coordonnées inversées : latitude et longitude dans le mauvais ordre](https://quickwell.app/fr/learn/eudr/swapped-coordinates/): En GeoJSON, chaque position s'écrit [longitude, latitude]. Les fichiers issus de tableurs inversent souvent l'ordre et placent les parcelles dans un autre pays ou en mer. Comment repérer et corriger sans risque.
- [Décimales : au moins 6, et l'effet de la troncature sur vos polygones](https://quickwell.app/fr/learn/eudr/six-decimal-places/): La géolocalisation RDUE exige au moins 6 décimales, et le Système d'information de l'UE tronque tout ce qui dépasse 6. Pourquoi trop peu de décimales posent problème et comment la troncature crée des points en double.
- [Polygone non fermé : le premier et le dernier point doivent être identiques](https://quickwell.app/fr/learn/eudr/unclosed-polygon/): Chaque polygone de parcelle RDUE doit être fermé : la première et la dernière paire de coordonnées doivent être identiques, avec au moins quatre positions. Pourquoi les polygones restent ouverts et comment les fermer.
- [Polygone auto-sécant : lignes qui se croisent, formes en huit et pointes](https://quickwell.app/fr/learn/eudr/self-intersecting-polygon/): Le Système d'information de l'UE refuse les polygones de parcelle dont les côtés se croisent (forme en huit), se replient sur eux-mêmes ou forment des pointes. Pourquoi, pourquoi ne pas corriger automatiquement, et comment relever à nouveau.
- [Polygones avec trous refusés : la solution des deux moitiés](https://quickwell.app/fr/learn/eudr/polygon-holes/): Le Système d'information de l'UE n'accepte pas les polygones avec trous (formes en anneau). Pourquoi des parcelles ont des trous et la solution officielle : décrire la parcelle par deux demi-anneaux.
- [Points et règle des 4 hectares : quand une parcelle exige un polygone](https://quickwell.app/fr/learn/eudr/point-area-over-4-hectares/): Dans la géolocalisation RDUE, un point peut représenter une parcelle de 4 hectares au plus ; au-delà, il faut un polygone, sauf pour les bovins. Comment le système lit la propriété Area, sa valeur par défaut de 4 ha et son minimum.
- [LineString et MultiLineString ne sont pas acceptées pour les parcelles](https://quickwell.app/fr/learn/eudr/linestring-not-accepted/): Le Système d'information de l'UE n'accepte pas les géométries LineString ou MultiLineString comme lieux de production. Pourquoi les applications GPS exportent des lignes et comment transformer un contour relevé en polygone valide.
- [GeometryCollection dans les fichiers RDUE : acceptée, mais vérifiez son contenu](https://quickwell.app/fr/learn/eudr/geometrycollection/): Le Système d'information de l'UE accepte la GeometryCollection, mais une collection qui contient des lignes, ou qui mélange points et polygones, crée des erreurs. Comment la remplacer par un MultiPolygon ou un MultiPoint.
- [Noms de propriétés : ProducerName, ProducerCountry, ProductionPlace, Area](https://quickwell.app/fr/learn/eudr/property-names/): Le Système d'information de l'UE lit quatre propriétés GeoJSON facultatives, dont les noms sont sensibles à la casse : ProducerName, ProducerCountry (code ISO à 2 lettres), ProductionPlace et Area. Erreurs fréquentes et corrections.
- [Limites de taille et de volume : 25 Mo par déclaration, 1 000 producteurs par marchandise](https://quickwell.app/fr/learn/eudr/file-size-limit/): Le Système d'information de l'UE limite les données de géolocalisation à 25 Mo par déclaration, et les producteurs à 1 000 par marchandise et 10 000 par déclaration. Comment alléger un fichier de parcelles sans perdre en précision.

## Texas RRC districts

- [Texas drilling permits by RRC district](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/): All 13 Railroad Commission of Texas oil and gas districts (01–10, 6E, 7B, 7C, 8A): the counties in each, district offices, major formations, recent permit counts and how to watch new drilling permits.
- [RRC District 01 (San Antonio): counties, drilling permits and how to watch them](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/district-01/): Railroad Commission of Texas oil and gas District 01: all 33 counties, the San Antonio district office, major formations, permit counts for July–September 2026, and how to follow new drilling permits.
- [RRC District 02 (San Antonio): counties, drilling permits and how to watch them](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/district-02/): Railroad Commission of Texas oil and gas District 02: all 10 counties, the San Antonio district office, major formations, permit counts for July–September 2026, and how to follow new drilling permits.
- [RRC District 03 (Houston): counties, drilling permits and how to watch them](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/district-03/): Railroad Commission of Texas oil and gas District 03: all 29 counties, the Houston district office, major formations, permit counts for July–September 2026, and how to follow new drilling permits.
- [RRC District 04 (Corpus Christi): counties, drilling permits and how to watch them](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/district-04/): Railroad Commission of Texas oil and gas District 04: all 15 counties, the Corpus Christi district office, major formations, permit counts for July–September 2026, and how to follow new drilling permits.
- [RRC District 05 (Henderson): counties, drilling permits and how to watch them](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/district-05/): Railroad Commission of Texas oil and gas District 05: all 24 counties, the Henderson district office, major formations, permit counts for July–September 2026, and how to follow new drilling permits.
- [RRC District 06 (Henderson): counties, drilling permits and how to watch them](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/district-06/): Railroad Commission of Texas oil and gas District 06: all 23 counties, the Henderson district office, major formations, permit counts for July–September 2026, and how to follow new drilling permits.
- [RRC District 6E: the East Texas Field district](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/district-6e/): RRC oil and gas District 6E covers the East Texas Field, in Gregg, Rusk, Upshur, Cherokee and Smith counties. Why it has no counties of its own in the RRC county table, how 6E shows up in permit data, and how to watch permits there.
- [RRC District 7B (Abilene): counties, drilling permits and how to watch them](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/district-7b/): Railroad Commission of Texas oil and gas District 7B: all 24 counties, the Abilene district office, major formations, permit counts for July–September 2026, and how to follow new drilling permits.
- [RRC District 7C (San Angelo): counties, drilling permits and how to watch them](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/district-7c/): Railroad Commission of Texas oil and gas District 7C: all 14 counties, the San Angelo district office, major formations, permit counts for July–September 2026, and how to follow new drilling permits.
- [RRC District 08 (Midland): counties, drilling permits and how to watch them](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/district-08/): Railroad Commission of Texas oil and gas District 08: all 20 counties, the Midland district office, major formations, permit counts for July–September 2026, and how to follow new drilling permits.
- [RRC District 8A (Lubbock): counties, drilling permits and how to watch them](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/district-8a/): Railroad Commission of Texas oil and gas District 8A: all 21 counties, the Lubbock district office, major formations, permit counts for July–September 2026, and how to follow new drilling permits.
- [RRC District 09 (Wichita Falls): counties, drilling permits and how to watch them](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/district-09/): Railroad Commission of Texas oil and gas District 09: all 15 counties, the Wichita Falls district office, major formations, permit counts for July–September 2026, and how to follow new drilling permits.
- [RRC District 10 (Pampa): counties, drilling permits and how to watch them](https://quickwell.app/learn/texas-drilling-permits/district-10/): Railroad Commission of Texas oil and gas District 10: all 26 counties, the Pampa district office, major formations, permit counts for July–September 2026, and how to follow new drilling permits.
